summary: The file area shows placeholders only until a search's first answer is in. After that, a search that runs again leaves what is there: the results, or the message when there are none, so typing on after "No Results" no longer flashes placeholder bars on every letter and "Indexing…" no longer blinks each time the search is tried again. A contents search running again after it found nothing reads "Searching…" until it answers. The first letter of a search and a switch between Name and Contents take the old rows away at once (the folder's items, or what the other kind found), and placeholders show until the results come. An answer from an index that was still being built reads "Indexing…" even when the status poll shows no scan, which covers the first search of a folder outside the search locations. A Nushell filter is not run over the empty rows of a search that has not answered.
changelog: After a search found nothing, every further letter flashed placeholder bars in place of "No Results" until the next answer came, and "Indexing…" blinked the same way while the index was being built. The message now stays where it is while the search runs again; a contents search, which can take seconds, reads "Searching…" meanwhile. A search also no longer shows items that aren't its results while it waits for them: the folder's items after the first letter, or names under the Match header and matching lines under Folder after a switch between Name and Contents. Placeholders show until the results are in. The first search of a folder outside the search locations says "Indexing…" while its index is built, where it said "No Results".
behaviour_changes: A search that runs again while nothing is listed keeps its message instead of drawing 14 placeholder bars (list) or 18 tiles (icons, gallery): "No Results" for a name search, "Indexing…" while an index is being built. This holds for typing on, Refresh, a scope or kind change, a filter turned on or off, a search setting changed, the retry while indexing, and the reload after another pane changes files. For a name search the kept "No Results" can be about the words as they were, for the tens of milliseconds the new search takes.

New message "Searching…" with the detail "Looking inside files for a match.": a contents search running again after an answer that left nothing to list, when nothing is being indexed. On a fast contents search it alternates with "No Results" on each letter, which the brief accepted.

First letter of a search (typed, sent to an open window by fff gui or a second launch, or a Smart Folder): the items shown before go at once and placeholders show until the first answer, about 55 to 85 ms for a name search and up to the time limit for a contents search. Before, they stayed and were drawn as results, with a Folder or Match column in the list; in column view the folder's items appeared as a list.

Switching between Name and Contents during a search: the results go at once and placeholders show until the answer. The selection is cleared at the click; before, an item both searches found stayed selected. The path bar, the preview pane and Quick Look lose that item at the click.

While waiting in the two cases above the status bar says "0 items" with the spinner (before: the count of the rows that stayed), and after a switch the timing is gone until the answer. fff's report of all items is empty in that time instead of listing rows that weren't results, and those rows can no longer be clicked.
A letter typed and deleted before the answer shows placeholders for that moment, then the folder again.

"Indexing…" with the detail "Results appear when indexing finishes." (no file count) when the last answer came from an index still being built and the status poll shows no scan: the first search of a folder outside the search locations (before: "No Results" for 600 ms, then placeholders, then the results); a rescan fff-search starts itself, or the first 400 ms after Rescan; and the one search right after a scan ends, which for a contents search lasts as long as that search.

With a Nushell filter on, no filter run starts over the empty rows of a search that has not answered: no spinner in the filter bar for it, and the keep-set of the list before stays, so deleting the letter brings the folder's filtered items back without a new run. When the rows were rebuilt before the first answer (a folder listing or an earlier filter run finishing), the first results are no longer all hidden until their own run ends.
The message title has an accessibility label equal to its text, as the status text has.
Manual: a "Searching…" row and a sentence on the "Indexing…" row in the table of file-area messages, and a paragraph under Searching on placeholders and on messages staying put.

Unchanged: Return and Down Arrow in the search field still wait for the results (search-enter-before-results), now with placeholders on screen instead of the old rows, also after a switch between Name and Contents.
left_out: CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.

No test of "Indexing…" with its file count staying put while a search location itself is being indexed: the harness waits for the index before it opens the window. The message without a count is tested through a folder outside the search locations, for the first answer and for a search running again.
The selection is not carried across a Name/Contents switch; it is cleared with the rows.
The scroll position is not reset when the rows are dropped; results-scroll-reset is its own brief.

examples/screenshot.rs is not extended. In-flight pictures need a temporary patch (--unsettled, and hold / tick:<ms> steps), saved at /home/user/polish-tools/shots/search-skeleton-flash-unsettled.patch; it applies to this commit.

The plan's bare rows.is_empty() return in apply_filter_to was narrowed to a search that has not answered. The bare form would also have stopped "Nushell (nu) was not found" from showing in an empty folder and left a running filter uncancelled when a list empties.
cargo clippy --features term was not run: src/term is untouched and no signature it calls changed.

Not compiled for macOS or Windows, and not without the test-support feature (the app's own build): check.sh builds all targets, which turns that feature on. The new ids copy the status-text element in bars.rs, which is built both ways.
README.md is unchanged: it states nothing this affects.
tests: tests/controls.rs: a_filter_waits_for_the_rows_a_search_has_yet_to_find (skips when nu is not installed)
Test ids added: skeleton (the placeholders' container, both layouts) and message-title (aria label = the title). Test hook added: Finder::search_in_flight_for_test.
review_fixes: Added tests/controls.rs indexing_stays_while_the_search_is_tried_again. The brief's second problem, "Indexing…" blinking against placeholders each time the search is tried again, had no test: with the rule changed to draw placeholders again whenever the last answer came from an index still being built (the plan of record asked for that when the status poll showed no scan), all seven of the implementer's tests still passed. The new test searches a folder outside the search locations, and while its first answer says "Indexing…" runs the search again with Refresh and looks before that search answers: no placeholders, and the title is still "Indexing…". It fails under that changed rule and when the message without a count is removed. Like the test before it, it checks this only when the first answer came before the index was built, which is nearly always; otherwise it passes without checking.
Nothing else was changed. The code, the manual text and the commit message are the implementer's.
notes:
Checked. The seven tests the implementer wrote each fail with the behaviour reverse-applied and only the test ids and the test hook kept (the tests don't compile without those): the folder's four items after the first letter, name rows after a switch to Contents (also in the Return test), placeholders at no results, placeholders where "Searching…" should be, "No Results" where "Indexing…" should be, and the folder's items with a filter on. With the filter guard and the message without a count removed, a_filter_waits…, a_folder_whose_index… and indexing_stays… fail and the rest pass. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit: 452 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. The two tests that search a folder outside the search locations passed 12 more runs with different seeds. Throwaway probes, not kept: a window opened with words to search for (Finder::new now rebuilds the rows inside the constructor, on the --query path no test covers) shows its results; with a filter on, a letter typed and deleted brings the folder's filtered items back at once with no filter run; gallery and column views show placeholders and come back; Refresh and a scope change at no results in Contents read "Searching…". My own pictures (review-*) show the in-flight frames in icons, list, gallery, columns and split view.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code says. (1) A key pressed while the rows are gone is lost: Return and Down Arrow go through results_pending(), true while a search runs, so they wait; the rebuild inside set_search_contents happens before run_search sets searching, and finish_enter checks again after it. (2) A message that is false or never leaves: every answer with indexing set is followed in the same task by the retry, unless a newer search replaced it or the search ended, and both reset what the message reads; "Searching…" needs searching, which only the matching answer or the end of the search clears. (3) A filter that hides or shows the wrong rows: the guard only skips a run over no rows before the first answer and leaves filter_source and filter_keep alone, so the first answer starts its run exactly as before.

One doubt for the owner: placeholders at the first letter of a name search. The plan of record asked for them and Finder also empties the window at once, but it is a flash of about 55 to 85 ms at the start of every search, most visible in icon view, where the folder's items used to stay and looked no different from results. If it reads worse on a real display, limit the drop in set_query to contents searches (if self.search_contents, call drop_stale_results; otherwise only clear the selection as before) and adjust the_first_letter_of_a_search_takes_the_folders_items_away, a_filter_waits_for_the_rows_a_search_has_yet_to_find and the manual's sentence.

For briefs still to come:
- empty-state-messages: the message branch of render_content is now rows.is_empty() && !loading && !awaits_first_results(), so the message stays up while a search runs again; three tests pin that. Add your !is_filtering() to that condition, don't put !searching back. The match has two new arms: "Indexing…" without a count when search_stats.indexing (your rule b is in, with the text "Results appear when indexing finishes."), and "Searching…" for a contents search in flight, which your empty_state needs as an input (searching) and a rule. The title already has the id message-title with an aria label and test_support; use it instead of adding empty-title. The manual's table has a new "Searching…" row.
- adhoc-index-feedback: your item 6 is done here (the message stays through each rerun when the last answer said indexing) and a temporary index no longer says "No Results"; your temporary flag only has to change the wording of the arm without a count. Two tests search a folder outside the search locations (a_folder_whose_index_is_still_being_built_doesnt_say_no_results, indexing_stays_while_the_search_is_tried_again); the first waits for the index with Engine::prepare and then gives the retry five settles, so a faster retry is fine.
- collapsed-groups-empty-view: same branch; put shows_nothing() in place of rows.is_empty() in both places and keep !awaits_first_results(). The new guard in apply_filter_to looks at the rows before grouping.
- results-scroll-reset: set_query's !was_searching branch now ends in drop_stale_results (clears results, search_stats and the selection, rebuilds the rows), so capture the folder's place before that call. set_search_contents does the same when a search is showing, so the selection is already cleared at the click. The lists aren't drawn while placeholders show.
- search-truncation-honesty: your "stopped" title goes into the same match; put it after "Indexing…" and "Searching…" and before "No Results". search_stats is None from the first letter, or a Name/Contents switch, until the answer.
- cancel-content-search: "Searching…" and the placeholders both read self.searching, so a search you abort must still be followed by the answer of the one that replaced it, or by set_query's empty branch.
- live-search-results: a quiet rerun that doesn't set searching shows neither placeholders nor "Searching…", which is what you want; a first run must still set searching, or the file area says "No Results" before the answer.
- back-forward-restore-search: restore_search sets search_contents and then calls set_query, which drops the old rows only when no search was showing. Going from one search to another of the other kind, call drop_stale_results (or go through set_search_contents) or name rows sit under Match until the answer.
- regex-content-search: don't copy the drop_stale_results call into set_search_regex; the rows stay matching lines.
- quick-look-empty-state: a Name/Contents switch now clears the selection, so Quick Look and the preview pane reach their empty state at that click too.
- content-match-highlight, preview-jump-to-match: results is emptied at a Name/Contents switch, so nothing stale sits there between the click and the answer.
- smart-folder-save-and-leaks: open_smart_folder writes search_contents directly; that is fine because it ends the search first, so set_query drops the rows. Keep that order.
- view-switch-keeps-selection: placeholders now show at the start of every search and after a Name/Contents switch, so the icon view goes undrawn more often than at no results and while loading.
- query-scope-from-cli: open_request's set_query empties the rows at once when no search was showing; a test that looks before settling sees none.
- search-syntax-click-example: set_search_contents(false, cx) during a search drops the rows and searches; the set_query after it searches again. One search more, nothing else.
- restore-session-tabs: a browser created with a query runs set_query, and with it rebuild_rows, inside Finder::new. That works; I tried it.
- Any test in split view: the ids message-title and skeleton repeat in the two panes, so scope the lookup.

Found, not fixed (all on the trunk before this change):
- Clicking the Name or Contents chip takes the keyboard out of the search field and gives it to nothing: letters typed next are lost and Down Arrow does nothing until the field is clicked or Cmd+F pressed (probe: after the click neither the field nor the files have the focus). The other chips are built the same way. It shows more now that the switch empties the list. Worth its own brief, near focus-lost-recovery.
- With a Nushell filter on, a search that comes back from no results says "No Results" until the filter's run over the new results ends, because apply_filter_to still holds the empty keep-set of the list before. empty-state-messages' !is_filtering() would cover the message.
- "Indexing… N files indexed so far" is chosen from the status of all search locations, not of the indexes the search used. A search of one finished folder that finds nothing says "Indexing…" for as long as any other location is scanning, and no retry is coming for it.
- files_changed (src/finder/trash.rs) asks the disk whether each search result still exists, on the window's thread, after every file operation during a search.

Not verifiable here: the look of the first-letter placeholders in motion, and the macOS and Windows builds.
